key_insight: Machine-learned long-time dynamics show that small polarons at oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110) are far less mobile than in the bulk because surface hopping pathways are strongly constrained.
engineering_relevance: This explains why porous rutile TiO2 can exhibit lower electron mobility than single crystals and informs surface/defect engineering for catalysis, photovoltaics, and energy-storage devices.
method: Extended machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics to a reducible oxide surface.
Ran several nanoseconds of finite-temperature dynamics on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110).
Analyzed polaron hopping pathways and vacancy-induced free-energy changes.
evidence_signal: The study reports nanosecond-scale simulations across multiple temperatures, revealing orders-of-magnitude lower surface polaron mobility than in the corresponding bulk and rare interlayer hops.
watch_item: The workflow depends on a transferable machine-learning model, so robustness should be checked when moving to other oxides, defect densities, or surface terminations.
paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
